hero.lead: A nation of 5.2 million with forest across six tenths of its land and almost all its power renewable, where the IMF approved a Flexible Credit Line in 2025 and the World Bank finances education and recovery.

register.name: First Fiscal Management and Green Growth Development Policy Loan
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 30 September 2025 · variable rate · 33.5 years, six years’ grace
register.note: Budget support for fiscal management and for jobs in rural and coastal areas
register.text: A World Bank development policy loan of US$300 million, approved by the Executive Board on 30 September 2025, to improve the efficiency of fiscal management and to promote sustainable economic activities that generate new jobs, especially in rural and coastal areas. It is a variable-rate loan with a final maturity of 33.5 years, including a six-year grace period; the jobs it supports serve the livelihood standard.

register.name: Social inclusion in the Emission Reductions Program
register.detail: World Bank · EnABLE grant · Approved 11 August 2025 · Environmental Bank Foundation (FUNBAM)
register.note: A grant for Indigenous Peoples’ access to the benefits of forest emission reductions
register.text: A US$4 million grant from the World Bank’s EnABLE trust fund for the National Project to Support Social Inclusion in the Emission Reductions Program, implemented by the Environmental Bank Foundation (FUNBAM). It finances rainwater harvesting, small-scale irrigation, training and land tenure security for the Cabécar, Bribri, Ngabe, Térraba, Boruca, Huetar, Maleku and Chorotega peoples, which serves the water and livelihood standards.

register.name: Flexible Credit Line
register.detail: IMF · Approved 2 June 2025 · two years · SDR 1.1082bn, 300% of quota · mid-term review 29 May 2026
register.note: Precautionary; access kept at about US$1.5 billion at the mid-term review
register.text: A two-year IMF Flexible Credit Line of SDR 1.1082 billion (about US$1.5 billion, 300 percent of quota), approved on 2 June 2025, which the authorities intend to treat as precautionary. At the mid-term review of 29 May 2026 the Executive Board found that Costa Rica continues to meet the qualification criteria and kept the current level of access.

register.name: Program for Sustainable and Competitive Agriculture
register.note: To benefit directly about 10,500 small and medium producers and their families
register.text: A Program-for-Results loan of US$120 million in support of the Public Policy for the Agricultural Sector 2023–2032, with disbursements tied to results in institutional modernisation, competitiveness, sustainable production and payments for carbon capture in coffee, livestock and sugarcane. It is to benefit directly about 10,500 small and medium agricultural producers and their families, which serves the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Results in Education (CORE)
register.text: Financing paid against results in schools.

register.name: Social Risk Management DPL with a Cat DDO
register.text: Budget support with funds that release when disaster strikes.

register.name: Climate Resilient Recovery and Territorial Development
register.text: Rebuilding roads, bridges and services to withstand storms.

register.name: Energy Security and Sustainability Program (SENSOS)
register.detail: CABEI · Announced 31 August 2026 · Moín dual-fuel plant, 200 MW · Río Piedras hydroelectric plant, up to 7 MW
register.note: 200 MW of baseload generation, and a hydro plant on the reservoir of the PAACUME water project
register.text: CABEI financing of US$485 million for the Energy Security and Sustainability Program in Costa Rica’s National Electric System: the modernisation of the Moín dual-fuel plant in Limón, adding 200 MW of baseload generation, and the Río Piedras hydroelectric project in Guanacaste, of up to 7 MW. The hydro plant uses the storage reservoir of the CABEI-funded PAACUME water supply project; the programme serves the energy standard.

register.name: Renewable Energy, Transmission and Distribution Program
register.detail: IDB · Reported 4 November 2025 · 23.5 years, seven years’ grace · SOFR-based rate
register.note: With a local contribution of US$115 million; about 40,000 street lights to LED
register.text: An IDB loan of US$200 million, approved by the Board of Executive Directors, to upgrade the Ventanas-Garita hydroelectric plant so that it can produce power for 30 more years, to modernise and expand transmission, and to replace about 40,000 conventional street lights with LED technology. The Costa Rican Electricity Institute (ICE) benefits, with a local contribution of US$115 million; the programme serves the energy standard.

register.name: Improving the Quality of the Educational System
register.detail: IDB · Reported 13 December 2024 · loan, with a US$7.5M grant from the Special Donations Fund
register.note: 1 million students and 90,000 teachers; the grant reaches about 49,000 migrant students
register.text: An IDB loan of US$150 million, with a non-reimbursable grant of US$7.5 million, to help the Ministry of Public Education modernise teaching, technology and administration, with catch-up programmes, curriculum reviews, teaching materials and stronger teacher training. It is to reach 1 million students and 90,000 teachers and to recover foundational reading and writing for over 111,000 students, which serves the education standard.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.

items.name: TECHO Costa Rica
items.text: An organisation that has worked for more than 17 years in Costa Rica’s informal settlements and built more than 2,000 emergency homes, with community centres and water systems. As a winner of the Citi Foundation Global Innovation Challenge 2024, it builds homes with rainwater collection, solar panels and a dry toilet for more than 250 people in rural Carrillo, Pococí and Los Chiles.

items.name: Banco de Alimentos de Costa Rica
items.text: A food bank that rescues surplus food from companies, checks and stores it, and distributes it through more than 365 social and community organisations in 69 cantons. In 2025 it received more than 3.5 million kilos of products, and it now reaches more than 44,000 people a month, among them more than 13,500 children.

items.name: ASONI (Asociación por la Sonrisa de los Niños)
items.text: An association whose Laboratorio de Sueños turns recycled plastic bottles into filament for 3D printers, from which it makes teaching materials and building blocks, so that young people from vulnerable communities build digital skills and creativity. It won in the social category of BAC’s Yo me uno awards in October 2025.

items.name: Asociación Moviendo Esperanzas (AME)
items.text: An association that manages biomechanical aids for people with disabilities and older adults; its project Esperanza Sobre Ruedas Verde y Digital modernises that work, with sustainable practices, in all seven provinces. It won in the social category of BAC’s Yo me uno awards in October 2025.

items.name: BIOSUR (biOsa)
items.text: A foundation of the South Pacific whose biOsa natural cosmetics empower women who keep native stingless bees in Rancho Quemado, Río Tigre and Puerto Jiménez, strengthening the local economy while conserving the bees. It won the Triple Value category of BAC’s Yo me uno awards in October 2025, with US$12,000 and support for its business plan.
